label: Argentina vs France
competition: FIFA World Cup 2022 · Final · Lusail Stadium

versions.label: Baseline — depth + inter-line
versions.note: Same classification logic as the other matches: back-line depth + inter-line compactness only. Unlike matches 2-4, this match's raw tracking DOES carry a per-player speed field (like the Morocco vs Spain baseline), so the pressure-on-ball-carrier score uses each player's own real tracked max speed -- see the methodology doc. One of the wildest finals in World Cup history: Argentina led 2-0, France drew level 2-2 in a two-minute Mbappe burst late in regulation, Argentina led again in extra time, Mbappe completed his hat-trick to make it 3-3, and Argentina won 4-2 on penalties.

The tracking is real 25 Hz optical data, resampled to the pipeline's 29.97 fps. The events are the DFL feed, snapped to the tracked ball. DFL has no analyst "under pressure" tag, so the engaged/passive threshold is pooled from the World Cup matches instead of calibrated on this one. The final day of the season: Bayern won 2-1 with an 89th-minute goal.
